name: Malayalam
signature: Highly rounded and loopy — full circles, hooks and curls, with almost no straight lines.
notes: Syllabary generated from Unicode by generate_syllabary.py: each syllable is a base consonant (varga order) composed with a core vowel sign. Romanization is ISO-15919. The independent (word-initial) vowels are in `independentVowels`; the script's own digits are in `digits`. Stroke order is a separate, source-gated effort: only source-verified entries carry it, beginning with independent short e എ. Parts, not the grid: handwriting is authored only for independent vowels, base consonants (the generated entries with a single `components` line), standalone chillu consonants, and vowel signs; a syllable's figure is assembled from its parts and is never authored separately. When `penLifts` is absent it means NOT VERIFIED — never none — and must never be inferred from the length of `strokeOrder`.

strokeOrderSource.variation: Jayasree records ൯ as one stroke: up the left side, over the arch and down the stem, back up it, over the second arch and down the right side through the crossing, round the bottom, then up through the crossing to the top right (start lower left, end upper right). The climb back up the stem retraces it. Jayasree keeps one recorded gesture per pen-down stroke, so one stroke means the recorder did not lift. Only these facts (stroke count, start, order, direction and end) are taken; no recorded coordinate is copied.
